#PLASTICKILLS #PLASTICKILLS 
On November 4, UMass Dartmouth students transformed the campus quad by spelling out #PlasticKills 
using bottles collected during shoreline cleanups with Be the Solution to Pollution. The installation, created 
in collaboration with Be the Solution to Pollution, MassPIRG Students, UMass Dartmouth Sustainability, and 
Sustainability 101 students under the guidance of Professor Rachel Kulick, highlighted the harmful impacts of 
single-use plastics on both human health and the environment. 
The project builds on earlier efforts to raise awareness about plastic pollution. In 2022, thousands of 
discarded alcohol nip bottles collected through Be the Solution to Pollution were used to spell out 
#BreakFreeFromPlastic, which later inspired the creation of the Sculpture Monster in 2024, a 60-foot-long 
sculpture constructed from 32,885 recovered nip bottles. Developed through a collaboration between Be 
the Solution to Pollution and UMass Dartmouth’s College of Visual and Performing Arts, the sculpture has 
become a striking symbol of plastic waste and is frequently featured during AHA!’s Earth Eve celebrations. 
Earth Eve Earth Eve 
On April 9, the annual Earth Eve Parade took place during 
New Bedford’s AHA! (Art, History, Architecture) Night. 
The parade brought together community members and 
creatively designed eco-floats to celebrate Earth Day and 
raise awareness about environmental stewardship. As 
participants traveled through the city’s historic downtown, 
they demonstrated a shared commitment to three central 
themes: reducing reliance on fossil fuels, celebrating and 
protecting the Earth, and embracing the principles of 
Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle. 
This year’s event also featured special recognition of 
Deirdre Healy, Retired Director of Community Service and 
Partnerships at the Leduc Center for Civic Engagement, and 
Bernadette Souza, Executive Director of Youth Opportunities 
Unlimited, who were honored for their contributions to the 
community and crowned the 2026 Planet Protectors.
